title: Lifebloom One to Improve Mobility in Older Adults in Nursing Homes
official: Contribution of the Lifebloom One Walking Service to Compensating for Disability in Older Adults With Reduced Mobility
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the Lifebloom One device improves walking ability in older adults with limited mobility living in nursing homes (EHPAD).

The main question it aims to answer is:

Is the proportion of participants whose walking ability improves with the Lifebloom One device, as measured by the Functional Ambulation Categories (FAC) scale, compared with their usual walking aid at baseline, higher than a predefined minimal rate below which the device would be considered futile?

Participants will:

* Complete 6 training sessions to learn how to use the Lifebloom One device
* Attend evaluation visits during which their walking will be assessed both with their usual walking aid and with the Lifebloom One device
* When applicable, use Lifebloom One therapy on their own within the nursing home between visits
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged 65 years or older
* Living in a nursing home (EHPAD)
* Dependent older adult with reduced mobility, defined as either: Requiring manual assistance or supervision from another person to walk 10 meters (FAC 1, 2 or 3), or Unable to walk even with manual assistance (FAC 0) but able to stand alone for 60 seconds (with or without a walking aid)
* Covered by the French national health insurance system (Sécurité Sociale)
* Able to understand the study and its implications
* Has given and signed informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Life expectancy of less than 3 months
* Lower limb amputation without prosthesis
* Pressure ulcers, wounds or medical equipment (e.g., insulin pump, colostomy bag) at the device's contact areas
* Blindness
* Major communication difficulties due to severe uncorrected deafness or mutism
* Any other condition preventing or compromising safe use of the device (e.g., Parkinson's disease stage IV, severe hemiplegia, recent major surgery, severe balance disorders, paraplegia, symptomatic orthostatic hypotension)
* Condition contraindicating cardiorespiratory exertion, or any other medical contraindication to physical activity
* Complete loss of sensation below the knee
* Contraindication to the sitting or standing position
* Body measurements not allowing proper fitting of the device:
* Excessive joint deformity or limited joint mobility of the lower limbs and/or trunk (flexion contractures, equinus)
* Not motivated to regain standing independence
* Contraindication to unsupervised use of Oxilio: cognitive impairment (Mini-Mental State Examination \[MMSE\] score below 10) and/or severe behavioral disorders preventing safe independent use of Oxilio
* Unable to understand the instructions for using the device
* Receiving psychiatric care, or under constraint or threat
* Unwilling to participate in the study
* Participating in another study aimed at rehabilitation
* Not willing to keep the Lifebloom One solution confidential
* Under court protection (sauvegarde de justice)
